'''Luigi Nicolais''' (9 February 1942 – 12 January 2026) was an Italian politician and academic, member of the [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]] and President of the [[National Research Council (Italy)|National Research Council]] from 2012 to 2016.

==Life and career==
===Academic and research career===
A chemical engineer, Nicolais graduated from the Faculty of Engineering of the [[University of Naples Federico II]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ssip.it//wp-content/uploads/2018/05/breve-biografia-di-Luigi-Nicolais_2018.pdf|title=Biography of Luigi Nicolais}}</ref> Full professor of "Polymer Technologies" at the same University, as well as the author of over 350 scientific publications, he was Director of the Institute for Composite Materials Technology of the [[National Research Council (Italy)|National Research Council]].<ref name=":0" /> He was also a professor at the [[University of Washington]] and the [[University of Connecticut]].

In 2012 he was appointed president of the [[National Research Council (Italy)|National Research Council]], replacing the new [[Italian Minister of Education, University and Research|Minister of Education, University and Research]] of the [[Monti Cabinet]] [[Francesco Profumo]] and held the office for four years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://napoli.repubblica.it/cronaca/2012/02/18/news/al_parlamentare_nicolais_la_presidenza_del_cnr-30097337/|title=Al parlamentare Nicolais la presidenza del Cnr|publisher=[[La Repubblica]]|date=18 February 2012|access-date=15 September 2022}}</ref>

===Political career===
On 17 May 2006, Nicolais joined the [[Prodi II Cabinet|second Prodi government]] as [[Italian Minister of Public Administration|Minister for Reforms and Administrative Innovations]] and held the office for the whole [[Legislature XV of Italy|15th legislature]].

A candidate in the [[2008 Italian general election|2008 political elections]] in the [[Campania|Campania 1 constituency]] among the [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]] lists, he was elected for a seat in the [[Italian Chamber of Deputies|Chamber of Deputies]]. During the [[Legislature XVI of Italy|16th legislature]], Nicolais was a member and Vice-President of the 7th Commission for Culture, Science and Education of the Chamber of Deputies.<ref name=":0" />

Formerly close to the positions of former [[President of Campania]] [[Antonio Bassolino]], he was regional councilor with delegations to the University, scientific research and technological innovation to the Campania region from 2000 to 2005.

He was a candidate representing the [[Centre-left coalition (Italy)|centre-left coalition]] for the presidency of the [[province of Naples]], but in the 2009 administrative elections he was beaten by the [[centre-right coalition (Italy)|centre-right]] candidate Luigi Cesaro.

===Death===
Nicolais died in Naples on 12 January 2026, at the age of 83.<ref name=death>[https://www.casertanews.it/cronaca/morto-luigi-nicolais-carditello.html Morto Luigi Nicolais, è stato presidente della fondazione Reggia di Carditello] {{in lang|it}}</ref>
